audit_findings.title: The earnings anchor is stale and mixed with 2026 balance-sheet and share data
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2024 owner-earnings anchor drives operating value, while the bridge and share denominator use June 2026 amounts.
audit_findings.evidence: For 2025, we expect that revenue will increase driven by higher volumes.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing error, not merely a possibility: audited FY2025 results and first-half 2026 results were available. FY2025 net income was $2,873 million, $251 million above 2024, while first-half 2026 GAAP net income was $1,281 million, $237 million below the prior-year period; the corresponding owner-earnings effect cannot be determined without rebuilding the worksheet. Because every operating scenario is capitalized from the stale $1,331.9 million anchor, synchronized actuals could materially change the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Compute FY2025 owner earnings from the supplied 10-K, incorporate first-half 2026 filed results or an LTM measure under the same policy, and rerun all scenarios using the June 2026 bridge and share count.

audit_findings.title: Equity-method investments may be double counted
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $3.316 billion of 2025 equity-method carrying value, equal to $14.70 per valuation share and 13.8% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Conrail, TTX, and other equity-method earnings enter owner earnings through operating-cost offsets, while stakes_net adds investment value again in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: These amounts partially offset the costs of operating the Shared Assets Areas and are included in “Purchased services and rents.”
audit_findings.explanation: The record demonstrates that Conrail and TTX earnings are embedded in reported expenses: their 2024 earnings totaled $137 million, comprising $89 million from Conrail and $48 million from TTX. It also shows $3.316 billion of equity-method investments at year-end 2025 within a $4.162 billion stakes bridge. Whether every bridge component is duplicated remains unresolved, but the identified exposure is large enough to materially overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $4.162 billion stakes_net balance investment by investment. For each separately added stake, remove its earnings and related distributions or offsets from owner earnings, or remove the stake add-back, and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Eastern Ohio losses above recorded accruals are unbounded
audit_findings.mechanism: Additional settlements, penalties, remediation, monitoring, and legal costs would reduce future owner earnings or require a direct deduction from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: At this time, we are unable to estimate the possible loss or range of loss in excess of the amounts accrued with respect to the matters described above.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved present contingency rather than a demonstrated omitted liability. At June 2026, filed Incident-related legal and environmental liabilities totaled $371 million, and first-half cash payments were $322 million. Liability insurance coverage for the Incident was exhausted, while several proceedings remained open and excess losses could not be estimated. The record therefore cannot establish their magnitude or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Update each proceeding through the valuation date, reconcile the $371 million recorded liabilities to expected payments, identify any remaining collectible property or third-party recoveries, and stress-test incremental uninsured losses.

audit_findings.title: The 2024 anchor may retain unusually large railway-property sale gains
audit_findings.magnitude: $490 million pretax total property-sale gains; $327 million after-tax railway-line-sale adjustment, equal to 24.6% of the $1,331.9 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retained nonrecurring sale gain inflates anchor owner earnings and is capitalized throughout the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Gains from operating property sales amounted to $490 million, $43 million, and $76 million in 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Retention is not demonstrated because the owner-earnings worksheet was not supplied. If the disclosed $327 million after-tax railway-line-sale gain remains in the anchor, however, it represents nearly one-quarter of modeled owner earnings and is plainly capable of materially overstating operating value. The additional risk of also adding proceeds or receivables in the bridge remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace the full $490 million pretax gain through the FY2024 worksheet, remove the documented after-tax nonrecurring amount under the existing methodology, reconcile related cash proceeds and receivables against the bridge, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Office residual-value guarantee may create an omitted balloon claim
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $499 million gross, equal to $2.21 per valuation share and 2.1% of $23.944 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A probable guarantee payment would be a claim ahead of common equity requiring recognition in owner earnings or the equity bridge beyond the recorded finance-lease liability.
audit_findings.evidence: The lease contains a residual value guarantee of up to eighty-three percent of the total construction cost of $ 499 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 2026 filing supersedes the earlier lease description: the arrangement became a finance lease with a $115 million liability, and the residual-value guarantee was approximately $499 million; management determined that no guarantee payment was probable. Even treating the entire gross guarantee as an incremental equity claim would reduce the $106.13 base value by only $2.21 per share, leaving it far below the $329.92 market price and not changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the guarantee is already reflected in the finance-lease economics and monitor probability, collateral value, and end-of-term settlement estimates; rerun only if a material payment becomes probable.

audit_findings.title: The PSU ceiling may not cover performance-based overdelivery
audit_findings.mechanism: Settlement above one share per reported PSU would increase fully diluted shares and reduce per-share intrinsic value.
audit_findings.evidence: PSUs provide for awards based on the achievement of certain predetermined corporate performance goals at the end of a three-year cycle and are settled through the issuance of shares of Common Stock.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed record identifies 118,888 PSUs at December 2025 plus 78,986 grants in first-half 2026, together equal to 197,874 target units or 0.088% of the 225.618 million-share valuation denominator before any multiplier. That target-unit scale is small, but the contractual maximum, modifiers, forfeitures, and merger change-in-control treatment are absent, so excess dilution cannot be bounded and materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the governing PSU award agreements for maximum payout, performance and market-condition multipliers, forfeitures, and change-in-control treatment; then replace target units with maximum issuable shares and rerun per-share values.
